nodes.description: CIDEC and PLIN1 act at the adipocyte lipid droplet itself. CIDEC is required for unilocular lipid droplet formation and for optimal energy storage in human fat; the truncating allele is mistargeted and fails to increase lipid droplet size, and the patient's white adipocytes are multiloculated (FPLD5). PLIN1 coats the droplet, and the FPLD4 frameshift alleles extend its C-terminus and act dominant-negatively rather than by haploinsufficiency.

evidence.reference_title: Partial lipodystrophy and insulin resistant diabetes in a patient with a homozygous nonsense mutation in CIDEC.
evidence.snippet: In addition to describing a novel autosomal recessive form of familial partial lipodystrophy, these observations also suggest that CIDEC is required for unilocular lipid droplet formation and optimal energy storage in human fat.

evidence.reference_title: Partial lipodystrophy and insulin resistant diabetes in a patient with a homozygous nonsense mutation in CIDEC.
evidence.snippet: we describe a female patient with partial lipodystrophy (affecting limb, femorogluteal and subcutaneous abdominal fat), white adipocytes with multiloculated lipid droplets and insulin-resistant diabetes, who was found to be homozygous for a premature truncation mutation in the lipid droplet protein cell death-inducing Dffa-like effector C (CIDEC) (E186X).

nodes.description: Three curated genes disturb the release of stored triglyceride from the adipocyte droplet, in opposite directions, which is why the node is tagged abnormal rather than increased or decreased. PLIN1 frameshift mutants fail to hold ABHD5, so adipose triglyceride lipase is constitutively activated and basal lipolysis runs unchecked (FPLD4). The reported ADRA2A variant removes the presynaptic alpha-2A adrenergic brake on adipocyte cAMP, again raising lipolysis, and is proposed to do so only in some depots (FPLD8). LIPE encodes hormone-sensitive lipase itself, so biallelic loss instead impairs triglyceride mobilization (FPLD6).

evidence.snippet: the p.(Val398Glyfs) and p.(Leu404Alafs) mutants fail to interact with ABHD5, leading to constitutive activation of adipocyte triglyceride lipase

evidence.reference_title: Whole-exome sequencing identifies ADRA2A mutation in atypical familial partial lipodystrophy.
evidence.snippet: ADRA2A is the main presynaptic inhibitory feedback G protein-coupled receptor regulating norepinephrine release. Activation of ADRA2A inhibits cAMP production and reduces lipolysis in adipocytes.

evidence.reference_title: Whole-exome sequencing identifies ADRA2A mutation in atypical familial partial lipodystrophy.
evidence.snippet: the mutant ADRA2A produced more cAMP and glycerol, which were resistant to the effects of the α2-adrenergic receptor agonist clonidine and the α2-adrenergic receptor antagonist yohimbine, suggesting loss of function.

nodes.description: The unifying defect across FPLD subtypes is failure of subcutaneous adipose tissue to develop and/or store triglycerides normally, owing to disruption of adipogenesis, lipid-droplet biology, or adipocyte maintenance. This produces selective loss of subcutaneous fat from the limbs and gluteal region.
nodes.id: Impaired adipocyte differentiation and adipose storage capacity

evidence.reference_title: Familial partial lipodystrophy resulting from loss-of-function PPARγ pathogenic variants: phenotypic, clinical, and genetic features.
evidence.snippet: PPARγ plays an essential role in adipogenesis, stimulating the differentiation of preadipocytes into adipocytes. Loss-of-function pathogenic variants in PPARG reduce the activity of the PPARγ receptor and can lead to severe metabolic consequences associated with familial partial lipodystrophy type 3 (FPLD3).

nodes.description: AKT2 is a kinase of the insulin/PI3K-AKT pathway, and ClinGen's review of the reported evidence records that AKT2 signaling is important for adipocyte differentiation. The reported FPLD allele has little or no kinase activity, so insulin signaling fails in the adipocyte itself rather than only downstream of an adipose deficit.

(Adipocyte-specific Lmna-knockout mouse data supporting a cell-autonomous role for lamin A/C in adipocyte maintenance are summarized in the entry notes.)

nodes.description: PPARgamma is the master transcriptional regulator of preadipocyte-to-adipocyte differentiation. Two curated routes converge on reduced PPARgamma signaling: loss-of-function PPARG variants themselves (FPLD3), and biallelic PLAAT3 loss (FPLD9), which remodels white adipose membrane phospholipids and strongly lowers PPARgamma signaling without altering PPARG itself.

nodes.description: Missense variants clustered in the heterodimerization domain of the NOTCH3 negative regulatory region were reported in three unrelated FPL families. Patient skin fibroblasts show raised NOTCH3 RNA and protein and activation of widespread senescence pathways, which the authors propose as the route from unrestrained NOTCH3 signaling to loss of adipose tissue. This node records a single-publication mechanism; see the notes on the NOTCH3 genetic record.

evidence.reference_title: Loss of phospholipase PLAAT3 causes a mixed lipodystrophic and neurological syndrome due to impaired PPARγ signaling.
evidence.snippet: These findings establish PLAAT3 deficiency as a hereditary lipodystrophy syndrome with neurological manifestations, caused by a PPARγ-dependent defect in WAT differentiation and function.

nodes.description: PLAAT3 is a phospholipid-modifying enzyme expressed in neural tissue and white adipose tissue. Biallelic loss of function enriches white adipose membranes in arachidonic-acid-containing phospholipids and strongly lowers PPARgamma signaling, so the lesion is upstream of the adipogenic transcriptional program rather than in it. This is the FPLD9 route.
